channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Angola plots mega investments in diamonds as talks with UK top miner begin
item.description: Angola is seeking to acquire a 20-30 percent stake in De Beers, the global diamond giant owned by United Kingdom-based firm Anglo American, as African diamond-producing nations explore a coordinated strategy to gain greater control over the industry’s most valuable assets.

item.title: Uganda’s central bank holds its key interest rate at 9.75% as inflation stays below target, while growth is supported by public investment and oil-related projects.
item.description: Uganda’s central bank has kept its key interest rate unchanged for the sixth meeting in a row, citing global economic uncertainty and still-subdued inflation.

item.title: Sudan pushes ahead with $1.5b Pakistan arms deal amid worsening humanitarian crisis
item.description: Sudan’s military authorities, under General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, are pushing ahead with a $1.5 billion arms agreement with Pakistan, even as the war-torn nation grapples with a deepening humanitarian crisis that has displaced millions and strained regional stability across northeast Africa.

item.title: Mali sets up state-owned firm to oversee mining assets and raise state returns
item.description: Mali will set up a state-owned company to manage its stakes in mining firms, the council of ministers said in a statement.

item.title: Experts claim that South Africa’s richest man be ready to part with another iconic luxury brand
item.description: Industry speculation is mounting that Richemont, controlled by South Africa’s richest man, Johann Rupert, is about to part ways with Jaeger-LeCoultre.

item.title: South Africa’s farm exports hit $15.1bn record as US shipments slump
item.description: South Africa’s agricultural sector closed 2025 on a historic high, with exports reaching a record $15.1 billion, even as shipments to the United States fell sharply in the second half of the year.

item.title: Congo to enforce local ownership rules for copper and cobalt miners, rebalancing stakes of some global mining giants
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo will begin enforcing a long-dormant rule requiring mining companies to allocate part of their share capital to local employees.

item.title: IMF data compares Africa’s biggest economies in 1990 and 2026, showing how South Africa, Egypt and Nigeria dominate growth while the continent still lags global GDP expansion.
item.description: Africa’s economy has expanded sharply over the past 36 years, but the pace of growth has not been enough to transform the continent’s position in the global economy.

item.title: U.S. brings bitter rivals Morocco and Algeria to the table over Western Sahara talks
item.description: The United States said it convened rare talks between rivals Morocco and Algeria over the future of Western Sahara, as the Trump administration seeks to revive efforts to resolve one of Africa’s longest-running territorial disputes.

item.title: Arthur Eze’s Atlas Oranto loses gas block in Equatorial Guinea as Venezuelan projects face U.S. scrutiny
item.description: Nigerian oil magnate Arthur Eze’s Atlas Oranto Petroleum is facing setbacks in key energy jurisdictions, including Equatorial Guinea, Senegal and Venezuela, as governments and operators tighten oversight of strategic projects and licences.
